name: MTAP loss / CDKN2A homozygous deletion
summary: Homozygous deletion of the 9p21 locus (CDKN2A with co-deleted MTAP) is a frequent event in mesothelioma that supports malignancy and carries adverse prognostic significance, and MTAP loss creates a targetable PRMT5 dependency also relevant in NSCLC.
biology: CDKN2A encodes p16INK4a and p14ARF, which restrain CDK4/6-RB and MDM2-p53 axes. MTAP, adjacent on 9p21, salvages methionine; its co-deletion causes accumulation of methylthioadenosine (MTA), which partially inhibits PRMT5 and sensitises cells to MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitors and MAT2A inhibition.
alterations: CDKN2A inactivating mutations or promoter methylation (other tumour types)

methods: Fluorescence in situ hybridisation for CDKN2A homozygous deletion
Immunohistochemistry for loss of MTAP expression (surrogate for 9p21 deletion)
testing.specimen: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue or cytology cell block
testing.notes: MTAP IHC is a practical surrogate for CDKN2A deletion with good concordance; combining BAP1 and MTAP IHC increases sensitivity for distinguishing mesothelioma from reactive proliferations.

predictiveRelevance: Primarily diagnostic and prognostic in mesothelioma. MTAP deletion is being evaluated as a predictive biomarker for MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitors and MAT2A inhibitors across tumour types, including NSCLC and mesothelioma, but these remain investigational.
